entity.name: Falsify OÜ
entity.description: Falsify OÜ (registry code 17574308, Tallinn, Estonia) maintains PRML — an open specification (CC BY 4.0) for locking the success criteria of an AI/ML evaluation (metric, comparator, threshold, dataset hash, seed) to a SHA-256 digest before the evaluation runs, so any third party can later verify the pass bar predated the result. The company maintains the specification, four byte-equivalent reference implementations, a published conformance suite, and a public commitment registry with Ed25519-signed receipts, RFC 3161 timestamps, and mirroring to the Rekor transparency log. Sole maintainer: Cüneyt Öztürk.

projects.name: falsify / PRML
projects.description: PRML (Pre-Registered ML Manifest) makes AI evaluation claims tamper-evident: nine YAML fields serialized to canonical bytes and committed to a SHA-256 before the run. Verification is offline and deterministic — PASS / FAIL / TAMPERED as CI exit codes — and requires no server to exist. Four reference implementations (Python, JavaScript, Go, Rust) reproduce 21 conformance vectors byte-for-byte, checked daily in CI. The schema is in SchemaStore; the tool is listed in the UK AI Security Institute's Inspect extensions catalog; OpenSSF Best Practices 100%. Relevant to EU AI Act Art. 9(8), which requires testing high-risk AI against prior defined metrics and thresholds.

plans.name: Specification and implementations maintenance (12 months)
plans.description: Maintainer time on the integrity core: spec v0.2 → v1.0 candidate, conformance-suite hardening, key rotation and decade-scale archival verification, and keeping the four implementations, registry and adapters (MLflow, Inspect, Giskard, DeepEval) maintained and free.

plans.name: Independent security review of the registry and canonicalization
plans.description: External cryptographic review of canonicalization and commitment correctness, the registry worker (the only privileged component), and the honesty of the published threat model.

plans.name: Threshold-disclosure measurement series
plans.description: Annual re-measurement of pass-criteria disclosure in published AI-assurance case studies (2026 baseline: a reader can recover the decision rule in 3 of 29 published case studies — falsify.dev/notes/threshold-disclosure). Published openly, CC BY 4.0.
